newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil forecasters differ on outlook for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil forecasters differ on outlook for coffee.

text.p: Brazilian weather forecasters had mixed views on the severity of expected cold weather in the coming days for the country's coffee regions.

Independent meteorologist Somar predicted lows of five degrees Celsius in highland areas in southern Minas Gerais and north Parana and 10 degrees in other coffee regions for the early morning of June 8.
But a low pressure system expected to enter the country on the same day should mean that temperatures will begin to pick up again from the early morning of June 9.
Even in the coldest regions, Somar did not expect any damaging frosts in the coffee regions, saying there was only a the possibility of light frosts in low-lying areas which would not affect coffee.

National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet) predicted a colder outlook, with temperatures possibly falling to as low as zero degrees Celsius in the north of Parana from early Sunday morning and the approaching low pressure system only likely to provide cloud protection along the coast.

Simepar, a regional weather forecasting system in Parana, expects to see minimum temperatures of around four degrees in the north of Parana from June 8 and said that was a large chance of frosts in lower-lying regions. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
